metaData.originalTitle: 从 3632 个漏洞看 AI 时代的评测基准重构！VulnGym 基准发布
metaData.title: Rebuilding Evaluation Benchmarks in the AI Era: Insights from 3,632 Vulnerabilities and the VulnGym Benchmark Release
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tencent's Wukong Security Team, in collaboration with multiple universities, releases the VulnGym evaluation benchmark based on 3,632 real vulnerability data points, focusing on the rising trend of business logic vulnerabilities in the AI era, providing a project-level, white-box, path-level annotated vulnerability detection capability evaluation scheme.
metaData.summary: Based on a statistical analysis of 3,632 high-severity/critical GitHub Advisory vulnerabilities from January 2025 to April 2026, this article reveals a structural shift in vulnerability patterns in the AI coding era: the proportion of business logic vulnerabilities is continuously rising, reaching 47.2% in high-star projects by April 2026. The article analyzes the causes of this trend from two perspectives: the supply side (the proliferation of AI coding tools changing how vulnerabilities are introduced) and the detection side (AI security tools beginning to uncover previously hard-to-find business logic flaws). In response, Tencent's Wukong Security Team, in collaboration with institutions including the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, the University of Hong Kong, Peking University, and the Institute of Information Engineering at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, has released the VulnGym evaluation benchmark. This benchmark uses real vulnerabilities from high-star GitHub projects as its data source, covering over 400 vulnerability paths, of which 71.2% are business logic vulnerabilities. It employs path-level annotation with three key elements: entry_point, critical_operation, and trace, supporting reproducible and interpretable deterministic evaluations. It can be used to compare the vulnerability detection capabilities of underlying models, Harness engineering, and Agent tools as a whole.

mainPoints.point: Vulnerability patterns in the AI coding era are shifting from traditional coding errors to business logic flaws.
mainPoints.explanation: Statistical analysis based on 3,632 vulnerability reports shows that the proportion of business logic vulnerabilities in high-star projects has risen from 21.4% in the first three quarters of 2025 to 47.2% in April 2026, closely aligning with the timeline of AI coding tool adoption.

mainPoints.point: Existing vulnerability detection evaluation benchmarks suffer from a systematic mismatch and cannot effectively assess business logic vulnerability detection capabilities.
mainPoints.explanation: Mainstream benchmarks exhibit a systematic mismatch across three dimensions: evaluation granularity (function-level vs. project-level), vulnerability types (focusing on traditional CWEs rather than business logic), and evaluation format (black-box vs. white-box), failing to effectively assess project-level business logic vulnerability detection capabilities.

mainPoints.point: VulnGym adopts three-element path-level annotation, enabling differentiation between tools that merely guess a location and those that truly understand the vulnerability.
mainPoints.explanation: Each sample annotates three locations: entry_point, critical_operation, and trace, supporting step-by-step alignment of entry points, attack chains, and defect trigger points, making it the finest annotation granularity among current similar benchmarks.

keyQuotes: The profile of high-severity vulnerabilities in the AI coding era is shifting from 'traditional coding errors' to 'formally correct code with business logic flaws.'
LLMs excel at filling in 'plausible-looking' code but lack the long-term retention of project-specific business rules.
Enabling precise differentiation between 'a tool guessing a location' and 'a tool fully understanding the vulnerability'—this is VulnGym's finer-grained requirement at the annotation level.
Over the past decade, this yardstick has been repeatedly refined... each refinement of the scale corresponded to the true nature of code defects in that era.
As AI begins to deeply participate in code generation, are the types of vulnerabilities also changing?

relatedArticles.title: Beyond Cognitive Reconstruction: Stepping into the Engineering Revolution of Agentic Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a deep dive into the practical journey of Tencent engineers transitioning from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering, proposing an AI-assisted engineering system centered on context management and tool-oriented design.

relatedArticles.title: From Requirements to Deployment: A Comprehensive Leap in R&D Efficiency with Full AI Automation
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically explains how Tencent's audit team built a fully automated AI delivery platform to achieve end-to-end automation from requirements, design, development, testing to deployment, and shares its evolution path from L2 (human-machine collaboration) to L3 (full automation), along with core challenges, specific practices, and quantified benefits.

relatedArticles.title: Nanjing University Team Challenges High-Score Myth of Large Models: Human 90 Points, Strongest Model Only 49 Points
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: The Nanjing University team led by Fu Chaoyou released the new video understanding benchmark Video-MME-v2, which, through an innovative three-tier capability system and group-level nonlinear scoring, reveals a significant gap between the current strongest video models and human experts under rigorous evaluation, and finds that the gains from 'Chain-of-Thought' are highly dependent on textual cues.

relatedArticles.title: Deep Dive into Vaults: The Security Component of Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This post provides a detailed look at the Vaults component in Claude Managed Agents and its architectural design for secure user credential management.

relatedArticles.title: When Agents Truly Enter Complex Data Analysis Scenarios: DataClawBench Uses 492 Real-World Tasks for a Process-Level Examination of Frontier Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: DataClawBench is a data analysis evaluation benchmark based on 492 real-world financial think tank tasks. By retaining uncleaned data and hiding data source priors, it conducts a process-level evaluation of frontier large models, revealing their capability boundaries and failure modes in real exploratory analysis scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: When the Entire Team Goes Zero-Manual Coding: A 10,000-Word AI-Native Development Handbook
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the Tencent team's practical experience in transitioning from AI-assisted programming to an AI-native development model, achieving a 'zero-manual coding' development loop through the OpenSpec specification and CodeBuddy toolchain.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Can AI Write Code in Truly "Mission-Critical" Backend Systems?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the complete methodology—Harness Engineering—practiced by Tencent's CDN LEGO team for AI coding in ultra-large-scale, high-reliability backend systems. Through a five-layer architecture, three key levers (context, constraints, feedback), and multi-model adversarial code review, they built an engineering system that enables AI to safely and controllably produce high-quality code.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: The OpenClaw Ecosystem is Exploding: We Deconstructed Over 40 Related Products on Product Hunt
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth deconstruction of the AI Agent ecosystem built around the OpenClaw framework, covering five core tracks—social, memory, deployment, security, and hardware—revealing the trend of the internet shifting from "serving humans" to "serving Agents."

relatedArticles.title: CoPaw 1.0 Release: Comprehensive Evolution in Customized Small Models, Security Mechanisms, and Multi-Agent Systems
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: CoPaw 1.0 is officially released, creating a secure and controllable local personal AI assistant through customized small models, a three-layer security defense architecture, multi-agent collaboration, and ReMe memory management.
